finding.claim: /checkout computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty, allowing a user to pay 0 or a negative amount for goods.

trace.note: POST /checkout handler entered, no validation middleware
total = sum(i.price * i.qty) using raw client values
payments.charge invoked with the client-derived total

finding.guards_checked: No price lookup against catalog, no non-negative or type checks on price/qty, no minimum-charge check in this file. payments.charge implementation not present.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:5 sums req.body.items price*qty with no catalog lookup or type/sign checks, and cart.js:6 passes that total straight to req.payments.charge. The sibling /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14) looks up prices via req.catalog.price(i.sku) and clamps qty, which shows the legacy route lacks that protection. payments.charge is not in the directory, so a downstream rejection of zero or negative amounts cannot be ruled out.
verdict.reason: The attacker is any authenticated customer (req.user.id, cart.js:6), and cart.js:5 derives the charged total from client-supplied price and qty with no effective check before cart.js:6 charges it. The only unverified piece is whether payments.charge itself rejects zero or negative amounts, which is not in the available code.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 does not guard against NaN or Infinity in the total, so a malformed qty or an unknown sku can produce a NaN/Infinity charge.

trace.note: catalog.price(i.sku) may return undefined for unknown sku
Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) returns NaN for non-numeric qty; Infinity for huge qty

finding.guards_checked: Math.max(1, ...) clamps low values but does not reject NaN; no Number.isFinite check; no check that catalog.price returned a number. Behavior of payments.charge on NaN is unknown.
finding.repro: POST /checkout-v2 {"items":[{"sku":"A","qty":"abc"}]} -> total NaN. {"items":[{"sku":"A","qty":1e400}]} -> total Infinity (JSON parses to Infinity).

verdict.guard_found: None in cart.js. Line 14 (`Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty))`) clamps low values but returns NaN for non-numeric qty and passes Infinity through. There is no Number.isFinite or typeof check on qty or on the value from req.catalog.price (cart.js:13). The attacker must be an authenticated user (req.user.id at cart.js:16), but no auth middleware is in the repo to confirm that. The repo has no payments.charge or catalog.price implementation, so nothing shows how a NaN or Infinity total is handled.
verdict.reason: The trace lines match cart.js:13-16 and no validation exists in cart.js, but whether a NaN total causes harm depends on req.payments.charge and req.catalog.price, which are not in the directory. An Infinity total from a huge qty only overcharges the requester, so the real risk is a NaN charge that a processor accepts as zero, and that cannot be decided from this code.

finding.claim: A request without req.body.items throws inside an async handler; on Express 4 without a process-level rejection handler this can crash the process.
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection in async route handler (cart.js:4 and cart.js:10)

trace.note: req.body.items.reduce throws TypeError when items is undefined
same failure mode in /checkout-v2 for-of loop

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch, no schema validation, no Express error wrapper visible. Express version and process-level unhandledRejection handler are not in the directory.
finding.repro: POST /checkout {} -> TypeError from undefined.reduce; on Express 4 + Node >=15 with no handler, the process exits.

verdict.guard_found: None in cart.js: no try/catch around the async handlers at cart.js:4-8 and cart.js:10-17, and no input validation of req.body.items before cart.js:5 or cart.js:12. The directory has no app entry point, Express version, or process.on('unhandledRejection') handler, so an upstream error middleware or process handler cannot be ruled in or out.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:5 calls reduce on req.body.items and cart.js:12 iterates it with for-of, and neither has a guard in cart.js:4-17, so a missing items value rejects the async handler. Whether that crashes the process depends on the Express version (Express 4 does not forward async rejections, while Express 5 does) and on an unhandledRejection handler, and neither is in the available files, so the crash claim cannot be decided from this code.

finding.claim: The charge uses req.user.id without any check in this file that req.user is set and authenticated, so authorization depends entirely on an unseen mount-time middleware.
finding.source: req.user supplied by upstream middleware (not visible)
finding.sink: req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) at cart.js:6 and cart.js:16
finding.guards_checked: No authentication or ownership check in this file. Mounting code not present in the audited directory.
finding.repro: If the router is mounted without an auth middleware, an unauthenticated POST charges whichever req.user is populated or throws.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js. Both charge calls use req.user.id unchecked (cart.js:6, cart.js:16), and the only file in the directory is cart.js, so the mounting middleware that would authenticate req.user is not visible.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:6 and cart.js:16 call req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) with no check on req.user, but whether an anonymous attacker can reach them depends on auth middleware mounted outside this directory, which I cannot read.

finding.claim: Charge endpoints have no idempotency key or rate limit, so retries or repeated POSTs produce duplicate charges.

trace.note: no idempotency key read from request
each request performs a new charge

finding.guards_checked: No idempotency key, dedupe, or rate-limit middleware in this file.
finding.repro: Send the same POST /checkout-v2 request twice; two charges are issued.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js: no idempotency-key read, dedupe, or rate-limit logic at cart.js:4-18. The only file in the directory is cart.js, so app-level middleware or the payments client's idempotency handling (req.payments, injected elsewhere) cannot be checked.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:6 and cart.js:16 each call req.payments.charge with no idempotency key read from the request (cart.js:4-18), but the directory contains only cart.js, so an app-level or payments-client guard cannot be ruled out, and the attacker is just the authenticated user repeating their own charge, which is a reliability issue rather than a privilege flaw.
